approach: Held at constant volume while heated, the metal is prevented from expanding volumetrically; the bulk modulus converts that blocked volume strain into a pressure rise.

steps.text: Find the volume expansion coefficient from the linear expansion coefficient.
The blocked volume strain multiplied by the bulk modulus gives the extra pressure built up.
steps.why_this_step: Bulk modulus is the pressure needed per unit fractional volume change, so it converts the prevented volume expansion directly into pressure.

steps.text: Add the extra pressure to the initial pressure.
steps.why_this_step: The initial pressure of 10⁵ Pa is smaller than the rise by a factor of thousands, so it does not change the rounded answer.

common_mistakes.text: Using the linear expansion coefficient directly as the volume expansion coefficient, without multiplying by 3, gives 2×10⁸ Pa.
Using 2α, the coefficient for area expansion, in place of the volume coefficient 3α gives about 4×10⁸ Pa.
